compare page description: A line connects two foods when the upper one is at least as good on every selected nutrient and no worse on every cost (yen, CO2e, land, water) — a strict upgrade. Pairs with no line (e.g. organic vs conventional) are trade-offs; neither is simply better.
compare methodology note: Environmental impact figures are world averages by food category from Poore & Nemecek (2018); differences by origin are not corrected. Cost is a vector of (yen, CO2e, land, water), and the Pareto view keeps incomparable pairs. Health effects of pesticide residues are not quantified and are treated as "not assessed".

domination axes note: Axes: nutrient density per 100 g (protein, fiber, vitamin C) × cost (yen, CO2e, land, water). Domination = at least as good on every axis and strictly better on at least one.
See in the full Hasse diagram: See in the full Hasse diagram
hasse orientation note: Higher is better. A line means the upper food is a strict upgrade over the lower one (at least as good on every selected nutrient and cost, strictly better on at least one); pairs with no line are trade-offs. Click a food card to open its detail page.
scalarization intro: Environmental impacts (CO2e, land, water) are converted to yen and added to the price, producing a single ranking. Leave a slider at 0 to ignore that impact. There is no single correct rate — use the reference values under each slider as a guide and set them to match your own priorities.
co2e price reference: Reference: J-Credit market price ≈ 1–4 JPY/kg; social cost of carbon estimates ≈ 20–30 JPY/kg
land price reference: Reference: average annual farmland rent in Japan ≈ 5–15 JPY/m²
water price reference: Reference: household tap water ≈ 0.1–0.4 JPY/L (agricultural water is cheaper)
isolated foods heading: Foods not connected to any other food (every pairing is a trade-off)
